# Collective-Intelligence @ Stage 7 — Sentential & Faith

> developed 2026-07-26. Deepened from 73 to 140+ lines.

## Expression on this line

Collective-intelligence at Order 5 is **questioning collective behavior**: the first
moment where the agent evaluates its inherited collective rules against emerging evidence
and reasoning. "But is this coordination pattern really fair?" The child who asks "Why
do we have to share with the group?" is performing the cognitive operation that will
eventually produce collective intelligence theory.

The key advance from Stage 6 is **coordination-evaluation**. The agent can now step
back from its inherited collective rules and ask whether they meet some standard of
correctness independent of tradition itself. "Our tribe's custom of equal distribution
seems unfair in this situation" is a Stage 7 collective insight.

But collective reasoning at Stage 7 is still **concrete and particular**. The agent
can evaluate specific collective rules against specific criteria, but cannot yet
construct abstract theories of collective intelligence.

Faith-based collective behavior emerges at Stage 7. The agent chooses collective
patterns based on transcendent commitment: "We coordinate this way because it is right,
not because our ancestors told us." This is a genuine advance over Stage 6 — the
collective behavior is now chosen, not just inherited.

The transition from Stage 7 to Stage 8 occurs when the agent can construct abstract
theories of collective intelligence.

In human development, Stage 7 corresponds to the pre-teen who begins to question
group norms: "Why do we have to share but the adults don't?"

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** Cultural collective systems are now subject to internal critique.

- **UR:** The individual agent can evaluate collective rules against evidence and
  reasoning.

- **LL:** Institutions emerge that encode collective evaluation: schools of group
  dynamics, collective intelligence research, philosophical communities.

- **LR:** The library, the collective intelligence salon, the philosophical debate.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** Self-righteous collective imposition — forcing one's own collective
  evaluation on others.

- **Dark allergy:** Refusal to question inherited collective rules.

- **Golden addiction:** Clinging to one's own collective evaluation as the only valid
  perspective.

- **Golden allergy:** Rejecting all collective evaluation as subjective.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Coordination evaluation:** The agent evaluates collective rules against evidence
  and reasoning.

- **Faith-based collective behavior:** The agent chooses collective patterns based on
  transcendent commitment.

- **Concrete rule evaluation:** The agent can evaluate specific collective rules but
  cannot construct general theories.

- **Collective voice:** The agent challenges inherited collective rules when it
  perceives inconsistency.

## Sources, joints, open questions

**Sources:**
- Camazine, S. et al. (2001). *Self-Organization in Biological Systems* — collective
  reasoning as developmental achievement
- Bonabeau, E. et al. (1999). *Swarm Intelligence* — collective intelligence theory
- Wilson, E.O. (1975). *Sociobiology* — the evolutionary foundations of collective
  reasoning

**Open joints:**
